newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India, Pakistan growth seen at around 7 pct-UN unit.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan growth seen at around 7 pct-UN unit.

text.p: India and Pakistan should average annual economic growth of around seven percent between 1996 and 2000, the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) said on Wednesday.

The United Nations-affiliated commission's 1997 survey, released through Singapore's Trade Development Board, projected India's gross domestic product growth in the period at a flat seven percent, and Pakistan's at 6.7 percent.
"India, with its vast market size, skilled manpower and advanced technological base, is well placed to see further acceleration of its growth rates," the ESCAP report said.
"Pakistan's economy has a less diversified base than India's, yet it can realise its six to seven percent rates of annual growth beyond the year 2000."

The report cautioned that with "their vast populations, lower spread of basic eduation and generally low living standards for the masses, these countries may see social issues impose a greater constraining effect on the pace at which (economic) reforms could be implemented."

In other projections for south and southwest Asia, ESCAP forecast 5.8 percent average annual GDP growth in the period for Turkey, 5.7 percent for Sri Lanka, 5.1 percent for Iran, seven percent for Bangladesh, and six percent for Nepal.
